value.text: #ATproto already gives us the building blocks: AT URIs identify resources independently of clients. What if we had a shared linking and resolution conventions / features that allowed any compatible client to recognise those resources and open them natively?

Right now, if someone shares a link to @bsky.app content but I read it in say @mu.social , the link opens in my browser, not the app I'm already using. If I want to continue the conversation in Mu, I have to track down the same post or resource, defeating the purpose of links.

It would be cool to have client-agnostic linking across #ATproto . Links to posts, profiles, lists, feeds, etc. open directly in whichever compatible app the recipient uses, rather than forcing them into the app where the link originated, or a browser tab where they're not signed in.

Identities are issued as NFTs providing verifiable ownership, provenance and a permanent registration record, allowing identities to be transferred during acquisitions, establish ownership rights and create a standardised digital asset for every registered application.
